name: Wikipedia REST & Action API
summary: Article summaries, full-text search, page HTML and related content for every Wikipedia language edition.
description: Wikipedia content in 300+ languages via the RESTBase-style /api/rest_v1 endpoints (summaries, mobile HTML, random page, On This Day feed, pageviews metrics) and the MediaWiki Action API (query, search, extracts, categories, links, revisions). Summaries include a thumbnail, Wikidata ID and short description, which makes them well suited to entity grounding.

auth.notes: Anonymous use works; an optional OAuth2 token gives higher limits.

required_headers.name: User-Agent
required_headers.notes: Identify your app and give a contact; generic client strings may be blocked or throttled.

rate_limit.summary: Anonymous REST limits are generous (roughly 200 requests/second per client, from the research, not re-confirmed); Wikimedia asks for serial requests and low concurrency, and unidentified user agents get stricter limits (HTTP 429).

endpoints.summary: Short extract, thumbnail and Wikidata ID for an article
Full-text search via the Action API
Historical events on a given date

license.name: CC BY-SA 4.0 (text, also GFDL); Wikidata IDs and metadata are CC0

coverage.geographic: All Wikipedia language editions (about 7M articles in English)

agent_notes: Swap the 'en' subdomain for any language code. The summary response carries wikibase_item, which links straight to Wikidata. The Action API needs origin=* for browser calls and returns XML only if asked.
caveats: The older /api/rest_v1 is gradually being migrated to /w/rest.php and the api.wikimedia.org Core REST API, so prefer the newer documented paths for long-lived integrations.
Pageviews live on a different host: https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/metrics/pageviews/per-article/en.wikipedia/all-access/user/{Title}/daily/{start}/{end} (verified 200, CORS *).
